title: Slice-and-Verify release pipeline: ephemeral RC promotion, LTS lane assignment, and release notes delta automation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce manual overhead and risk in the weekly release train by creating an ephemeral 'slice-and-verify' pipeline that builds RC candidates, assigns them to LTS or rolling lanes based on change semantics, and generates a delta-based release notes draft for review. This ticket covers the orchestration glue, gating checks, tagging scheme, and release-notes automation.

Background:
- Current weekly cut requires manual candidate promotion, ad-hoc LTS assignment, and hand-edited release notes which slows down the cadence and increases churn when rollbacks are required.
- We want deterministic promotion rules and an automated delta release notes that surfaces user-facing changes and risk footnotes.

Acceptance criteria:
1) CI job (slice-and-verify) creates an ephemeral RC candidate artifact and a candidate manifest with commit/PR metadata.
2) Automated LTS lane assignment: patch-level changes (docs/strings, fix/bug) prefer LTS channel; behavioral/perf changes default to rolling; allow explicit override label.
3) Promotion flow: candidate -> canary (region-specific) -> global roll with configurable gating windows and automatic fallback to previous compatible model variant if health SLOs break.
4) Release notes draft created by parsing merged PR metadata, labels, and a delta of public API surface using the sdk-compat tool; draft is attached to the Linear ticket and created as a GitHub PR to the releases repo.
5) Rollback assistant triggered automatically on severe SLO regressions with a one-click rollback playbook in Console.
6) Instrumentation: telemetry dashboard shows candidate promotion latency, percent of candidates failing smoke/perf/regression checks, and mean time to rollback.

Plan / Implementation steps:
- CI: add a GitHub Actions pipeline (slice-and-verify.yml) that performs: build artifact, run smoke tests, perf quick-check (p99 latency), compatibility check, create candidate manifest and tag. Tag format: release/{YYYY.MM}-w{WW}-cand{N} (e.g., release/2025.01-w02-cand1).
- LTS assignment: implement heuristics in the release-orchestrator service using commit message prefixes and PR labels (e.g., label:lts-ok, label:behavior-change). Fallback to a ruleset maintained in repo config.
- Promotion gates: implement staged rollout controller with gates: smoke -> perf -> canary-regional -> global. Each gate reads SLOs from metrics-store and requires <5% error delta and <10% latency increase (configurable).
- Release notes: extend changelog-composer to accept candidate manifests and produce a delta view (user-facing changes, migrations, config impacts). Output to markdown draft and open GitHub PR to releases/release-notes with template.
- Console: add a candidate card and a rollout timeline visible in the Releases dashboard with promote/rollback controls.

Artifacts / Links:
- Orchestrator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-orchestrator/pull/289
- Changelog composer prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/changelog-composer/tree/feature/delta-drafts
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Release+Slice-and-Verify+Runbook
- Telemetry dashboard (dev): https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/RE/release-candidates

Open questions & trade-offs:
- Heuristic accuracy vs explicit gating: relying fully on labels risks misclassification; we will require an explicit override label for high-risk changes.
- How aggressive should auto-promotion be? We'll start conservative (manual approval after canary) and iterate toward auto-promotion once stable.
- Release note sensitivity: whether to include internal-only changes; composer will allow filters.

Definitions / Naming conventions:
- Candidate tag: release/{YYYY.MM}-w{WW}-cand{N}
- Lane labels: lane:lts, lane:rolling, lane:exp (experimental)
- Gate states: pending, pass, fail, degraded

Success metrics (first 3 months):
- 60% reduction in manual steps per weekly cut
- 50% fewer late-stage rollbacks caused by release note omissions or mis-tagging
- Mean time to promote candidate to global < 2 hours (after canary pass)
